svg.title: Wave properties of an electron and a photon
svg.desc: Top: an electron e−, a particle with mass, drawn as a sphere containing a wave, moves at speed v. Bottom: a photon, which has no mass, drawn as a wave packet, moves at the speed of light c. Both have wavelengths and both behave as particles. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Equal wavelength means equal momentum, not equal speed
Instantaneous phase profiles on a fixed 0.40 nm spatial span. λ = h/p for both particles; the
electron uses relativistic momentum. Curves do not show literal particle motion.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
